game: Week 8 2025 MIN@LAC, kickoff 2025-10-23 20:15 ET, venue roof dome, closing spread LAC -3, total 45.5, implied LAC 24.2 and MIN 21.2, weather forecast not saved

script.base: Thursday night Week 8 at the Chargers dome: LAC is a 3-point favorite in a 45.5 game, so the book expects a one-score script with LAC around 24 and Minnesota around 21, not a blowout and not a slog. Minnesota's offensive sample is weeks 4, 5 and 7 (no week 6, bye rest) and the rush log in that window is Carson Wentz 9 carries for 53, so J.J. McCarthy (Questionable, ankle) is not the base-case starter. Wentz's base lean is pass: Justin Jefferson 32 targets for 328 yards and 420 air yards, Jordan Addison 26 for 283 and 341 air, T.J. Hockenson 20 for 120, with Jordan Mason still carrying (44 for 166) because a 3-point spread does not force Minnesota to abandon the run and Los Angeles allows 5.20 yards per carry. Chargers base lean is Justin Herbert versus a Vikings defense that blitzes 47 percent, a split Herbert has played at plus 0.17 EPA per dropback versus plus 0.01 when not blitzed. The ball goes to Ladd McConkey (31 targets, 206 yards, 253 air in weeks 5-7), Keenan Allen (30 targets, 204 yards) and Oronde Gadsden (18 targets, 246 yards). Kimani Vidal is the recent Chargers carry leader (31 for 162 over those three games) if Los Angeles protects a late lead. Pace is moderate; at only -3, starters should finish.
script.flip1: Los Angeles jumps ahead by two scores early. Vidal and Omarion Hampton (12 carries, 44 yards in the L3, Haskins already Out) grind the clock, Herbert's attempts and McConkey's second-half routes stall, and Minnesota trails so Mason's rushing line dies while Wentz is forced into Jefferson and Addison. That flip saves a Jefferson over and kills a McConkey over if the lead comes before halftime.
script.flip2: Minnesota's tackles Brian O'Neill and Christian Darrisaw, both Questionable with knee injuries, sit or are limited, and the Chargers' 25 percent blitz actually gets home. Wentz is minus 0.25 EPA per dropback versus pressure, so Jefferson's 420 air yards collapse into Hockenson, Zavier Scott and Mason checkdowns. Mirror image: the Chargers' offensive-line cluster (Joe Alt, Trey Pipkins, Jamaree Salyer, Austin Deculus, all Questionable) sits, Minnesota's 47 percent blitz finally hits despite Herbert's season-long plus 0.17 versus blitz, and McConkey is stuck in the 11-to-39 yard band from earlier in the last four.

Zavier Scott Questionable (wrist) is the change-of-pace and receiving back (11 carries, 23 yards, 9 targets, 45 yards); if he sits with Jones also out, Mason is a bellcow and Scott's 11.5 rush and 31.5 rush-plus-rec lines are dead. Both starting tackles, O'Neill Questionable (knee) and Darrisaw Questionable (knee), are the offensive kill switch: pressure up, Mason efficiency down from an already modest 3.77 yards per carry, Jefferson deep air down, Hockenson and back catches up. The tackle and guard cluster Alt Questionable (ankle), Pipkins Questionable (knee), Salyer Questionable (knee) and Deculus Questionable (ankle) pushes Herbert toward quick middle throws if two or more sit, which feeds McConkey, Allen and Gadsden and cuts Quentin Johnston's downfield role (only 10 targets and 70 yards in three games). Safety Elijah Molden Questionable (thumb) is the deep-middle piece; if he is inactive, Jefferson, Addison and Johnston face a backup safety. Linebacker Troy Dye Questionable (thumb) would help Minnesota's tight end and backs (Hockenson, Mason, Scott) if he sits. Defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell Questionable (illness) would make a Chargers run defense that already allows 5.20 yards per carry and 29 runs of 10-plus in seven games even softer for Mason, but that is not a selected leg because Minnesota's own tackles are also questionable.

matchup.pressure: Chargers blitz 25 percent. Minnesota EPA per dropback is minus 0.25 when blitzed and plus 0.05 when not, so Wentz-to-Jefferson wants the quiet rush the Chargers usually play. Vikings blitz 47 percent. Chargers EPA per dropback is plus 0.17 versus the blitz and plus 0.01 with no blitz, so Herbert wants Minnesota to keep sending pressure, and Van Ginkel being Out makes that pressure less likely to arrive clean. The other pressure path is the Chargers' own questionable line (Alt, Pipkins, Salyer, Deculus) against that 47 percent blitz.
matchup.bleeds: Chargers run defense: 5.20 yards per carry, 29 runs of 10-plus in seven games, the clear run bleed, against a Vikings ground game that has only produced 3.77 yards per carry with Mason (44 for 166). Chargers explosives allowed: 17 passes of 20-plus for 235 yards in seven games, about 2.4 per game, not a broken deep defense. Vikings run defense is fine at 4.30 yards per carry and 22 runs of 10-plus in six games, so Vidal and Hampton do not have a soft front. Vikings explosives: 14 of 20-plus for 176 yards in six games. The pass bleed both quarterbacks can aim at is the middle, and Minnesota's 12.42 YPA on 36 middle attempts is the number that matters for McConkey, Allen and Gadsden.
matchup.overlap: Primary-target overlap for this specific game: Jefferson is Minnesota's top option (32 of 111 targets in the three-game window, 28.8 percent, 13.1 air yards per target) against a Chargers defense whose only soft pass zone is the middle at 8.66 YPA and that rarely blitzes, which is the split Wentz plays better. McConkey is the Chargers' top option (31 of 112 targets, 27.7 percent, 253 air yards) against the Vikings' middle at 12.42 YPA and a 47 percent blitz Herbert has already beaten at plus 0.17 EPA. Allen (30 targets) and Gadsden (18 targets, 13.7 yards per target) contest that same middle, so McConkey is the usage overlap and Gadsden is the explosive overlap, not a second leg. Mason overlaps the 5.20 yards-per-carry bleed but his own tackles are questionable and his recent yards sit on 57.5, so that overlap is noted and not selected.

pre_mortem: It is the morning after this Chargers home game and both overs lost. Jefferson finished 75 or 79 again because O'Neill and Darrisaw were inactive, Wentz took the minus 0.25 EPA blitz pocket, and Addison, who already has 26 targets and 341 air yards in the three-game window, caught the one or two explosives the Chargers allow (17 of 20-plus in seven games). McConkey finished 11 or 39 because Minnesota finally guarded the middle that has been at 12.42 YPA, Allen (30 targets) and Gadsden (246 yards, including a 164) ate the blitz-beaters Herbert usually finds at plus 0.17 EPA, and Los Angeles led by two scores so Vidal's 31-carry recent role closed the game. A fast Chargers lead is the single script that hurts both legs at once if Minnesota's extra throws go to Addison and Nailor instead of a Jefferson ceiling and the Chargers stop throwing. That counter-case is why Jefferson is flagged rather than sized up and why McConkey stays a lean. It is not stronger than the usage reads, so neither leg is cut before kickoff.
slip_story: One story only for this MIN@LAC ticket: a one-score dome game at 45.5 where both quarterbacks throw and the two primaries clear modest yardage lines. Minnesota's 21.2 comes through Wentz to Jefferson, the 32-target primary, against a Chargers team that blitzes 25 percent. Los Angeles' 24.2 comes through Herbert, who has been better when blitzed, to McConkey, the 31-target primary, against a Vikings middle at 12.42 YPA and a missing Van Ginkel. The two overs win together if the score stays inside one possession. They lose together if flip 1 hits and Vidal clocks it. Do not add Mason rush over, which needs a neutral or Minnesota-lead script the questionable tackles may not allow. Do not add Gadsden over, which cannibalizes McConkey and is inflated by 164. Do not add a total under, a touchdown, or a second market on either player. Two legs, no price, no parlay built beyond the story.
